approved: Tax Laws Amendment (Small Business Measures No. 3) Bill 2015

The speaker supported the Tax Laws Amendment (Small Business Measures No. 3) Bill 2015, which includes a five per cent tax discount for unincorporated small businesses up to $1,000 a year, immediate deductibility of professional expenses, and an expanded FBT exemption for work-related portable electronic devices. The speaker criticised the 2014 budget for damaging small business confidence and noted that the bill reinstates Labor policies previously abolished by the government.

The speaker supported the Tax Laws Amendment (Small Business Measures No. 3) Bill, which provides a 5% tax discount for unincorporated small businesses (capped at $1,000), immediate deductibility of professional expenses, and an expanded FBT exemption for portable electronic devices, as part of the government’s $5.5 billion Jobs and Small Business package. The speaker also criticised the opposition’s proposal to reintroduce a carbon tax via an emissions trading scheme and noted the repeal of the carbon tax in July 2014, a $50 billion budget repair package, and a business confidence index at +10 points.

The speaker supported the Tax Laws Amendment (Small Business Measures No. 3) Bill, which provides a 5% unincorporated tax discount capped at $1,000 per year for sole traders, partnerships and trusts, as part of the Growing Jobs and Small Business package. The bill also includes a reduced company tax rate of 28.5% for small businesses with turnover under $2 million, an immediate deduction for assets under $20,000, and other measures to reduce red tape and support the 8,955 small businesses in the Paterson electorate.

The bill introduces a 5% tax discount for unincorporated small businesses, immediate deductibility of professional expenses, and fringe benefits tax changes for work-related devices, with the technology sector predicted to add 540,000 jobs by 2033.

The speaker welcomed the Tax Laws Amendment (Small Business Measures No. 3) Bill 2015, arguing it supports small business as a key economic driver, and detailed coalition measures including cutting the small business company tax rate to 28.5 per cent for turnovers under $2 million, a five per cent discount for unincorporated businesses, increased instant asset write-off thresholds, and $70 million in accelerated depreciation for farmers alongside broader drought support funding.

The speaker argued in support of the Tax Laws Amendment (Small Business Measures No.3) Bill, part of the 2015 budget's $5.5 billion Jobs and Small Business package, which includes a five per cent tax discount for unincorporated businesses capped at $1,000 per year, immediate deductions for start-up expenses, and a fringe benefits tax exemption for portable electronic devices. The electorate of Higgins has over 20,800 small businesses, and the bill is expected to help over 400,000 women small business owners.

Argued in support of a small business tax bill offering a 5 per cent tax offset and immediate deductibility of expenses for businesses turning over below $2 million, part of the government's $5.5 billion Growing Jobs and Small Business package, and called for faster approval of the Adani Carmichael mine.

The speaker supported the Tax Laws Amendment (Small Business Measures No. 3) Bill 2015, part of the $5.5 billion Jobs and Small Business package, which provides a five per cent tax discount capped at $1,000 for unincorporated small businesses with turnover under $2 million, immediate deductibility of professional expenses, and an expanded FBT exemption for work-related portable electronic devices.

The bill provides a 5% tax discount for unincorporated small businesses (capped at $1,000 per year), immediate deductibility of professional start-up expenses, and a fringe benefits tax exemption for portable electronic devices. The member for Petrie supported the Tax Laws Amendment (Small Business Measures No. 3) Bill 2015, which introduces a five per cent tax offset on small business income capped at $1,000 for unincorporated businesses, and noted previous measures including an instant asset write-off for assets under $20,000 and a 1.5 per cent company tax cut for small companies with turnover under $2 million.

The speaker supported the Tax Laws Amendment (Small Business Measures No. 3) Bill 2015, which gives unincorporated small businesses a $1,000 tax reduction, immediate deductibility for start-up expenses, fringe benefit tax exemptions for portable electronic devices, and accelerated write-offs for water infrastructure. He noted over 2,000 job losses in his electorate of Grey from resource sector downturns, including lay-offs at Santos, BHP’s Roxby Downs, Alinta Energy’s Port Augusta closure, and Arrium’s Southern Iron shutdown.

They criticised the government for reinstating measures it previously cut, highlighted low start-up formation rates in Australia, and called for action on skills shortages, angel investor tax support, and equity crowdfunding legislation to better support the sector.

Labor will support the Tax Laws Amendment (Small Business Measures No. 3) Bill 2015, which includes a tax discount for unincorporated businesses, deductibility for start-up expenses, and an FBT exemption for portable electronic devices. The speaker argued the Abbott government's policies—such as cutting $845 million from industry support, reversing Labor's instant asset write-off, and creating economic uncertainty—have hurt small businesses, citing 800,000-plus unemployed, an 88% fall in renewable energy investment, and lost local procurement opportunities like Defence boots from Indonesia instead of Rossi Boots.
